correctness.rationale: Seven-state generator reward equations are derived and recomputed exactly from the stated transition intensities; their closed forms and the swap identity are symbolically verified. At fixed budget, expected extinction time is strictly increasing in the product ab. The occupied-time derivative has two positive roots by exact endpoint signs and Descartes, exactly one admissible; the sign under swapping excludes negative biases. Bounds, limiting biases and all boundaries are proved; twenty independent Fraction linear solves confirm the formulas on rational rate cases.

originality.rationale: Day and Possingham (1995) establish finite-state metapopulation transition-matrix methods but not the present continuous-time directional allocation theorem. Vuilleumier and Possingham (2006) was read in full and studies a different finite-horizon simulation objective. The 2015 spectral-radius work and earlier two-patch results do not imply the seven-state reward optimization. Classical contact-process transposition is explicitly treated as known. The strongly related 2010 article was available only as abstract, leaving historical-priority risk; no contrary coverage was found in accessible evidence.

value.rationale: Distinct, standard conservation objectives (time to extinction vs integrated occupied patch-time) select provably different dispersal allocations on the smallest nontrivial branching topology for every positive rate budget. The exact cubic gives a natural complete all-budget classification, unique optimum, bounds and limits. This is a structural objective conflict, not merely a trivial parameter substitution; the gain magnitude is acknowledged as modest for some budgets and no empirical impact claim is made.
